# R8 — V New Heaven and New Earth (21:1–22:5) + VI Epilogue (22:6–21)

**Range read in full:** cache slice lines 1–642 (source lines 6770–7411)  
**Source:** Osborne, *Revelation* (BECNT, 2002)  
**Section:** V New Heaven and New Earth 21:1–22:5; VI Epilogue 22:6–21

## Claims

### C1 — Section goal: final eradication of sin; promises to overcomers fulfilled
**Locus:** intro to 21:1–22:5 (slice ~ll. 3–7)  
**Quote:** "Since Adam and Eve lost their place in Paradise and sin reigned on earth (Rom. 5:12–21), the divine plan has prepared for the moment when sin would finally be eradicated… many of the promises given to the 'overcomers' (2:7, 11, 17, 26–28; 3:5, 12, 21) are fulfilled in this vision of the 'new heaven and new earth.'"  
**Claim:** For Osborne the whole Apocalypse aims at the new heaven/earth; Hemer is cited that heavenly Jerusalem’s perfection contrasts the seven cities’ imperfections; millennium reign is only a harbinger of greater New Jerusalem glory.

### C2 — Structure: thesis 21:1–8 expanded as Holy of Holies then final Eden
**Locus:** intro (slice ~ll. 7–8)  
**Quote:** "This section is organized like chapters 12–13, with a thesis paragraph (21:1–6, with 7–8 a parenetic challenge…) that is then expanded in two directions, first viewing the Holy City as an eternal Holy of Holies (21:9–27) and then as a new Eden (22:1–5)."  
**Claim:** OT images (esp. Isaiah, Ezekiel) prepare the day; heaven is viewed as earthly reality—city descends to earth; final Eden is “apparently in the ‘new earth’”; readers must choose overcomer vs coward (21:7–8).

### C3 — New vs first: qualitative newness (καινός); Jewish destruction vs renovation traditions
**Locus:** on 21:1 (slice ~ll. 48–50)  
**Quote:** "There is a major contrast between καινός and πρῶτος… with καινός emphasizing more qualitative newness than temporal newness… Two ideas predominated, one holding that there would be total destruction of the present world and virtually a creation de novo… and the other teaching a renovated or transfigured earth… Second Pet. 3:13; Rev. 20:11; and 21:1 follow the first tradition, as the old heaven and earth ἀπῆλθαν… have passed away…"  
**Claim:** Osborne surveys destruction-de-novo traditions (1 Enoch 72.1; 83.3–4; 91.16; 2 Bar. 44.12; Sib. Or. 3.75–90) vs renovation (Jub. 1.29; 4.26; 1 Enoch 45.4–5; 2 Bar. 32.2–6; T. Levi 18.5–10); places 2 Pet. 3:13 and Rev. 20:11; 21:1 with destruction/replacement. Affirms “some type of continuity within the wholly ‘new’ order” (physical resurrection; new earth) while uniting former heaven/earth dichotomy—heaven brought down to earth.

### C4 — Renovation vs replacement debate among modern commentators
**Locus:** on 21:5 (slice ~ll. 80–82)  
**Quote:** "There is a difference of opinion as to whether this 'new' creation means renovation of the old order (so Swete; Ford; Sweet; Wall; Harrington; Heide 1997: 43–44; Aune) or replacement with an entirely new order (so R. Charles, Walvoord, Beasley-Murray, E. Müller, Roloff, Krodel, Giesen, Mounce). As said above, there is both continuity… and discontinuity… but primarily the old was totally destroyed (as in 20:11; 21:1), and the new is a replacement."  
**Claim:** Osborne sides primarily with replacement; Isaiah 43:19; 65:17 support old gone forever; inaugurated sense in 2 Cor. 5:17 as harbinger of final new creation. Summary (slice ~ll. 112–114): debates over exact resurrection-body/heavenly physicality are “fruitless”—God says only it will be entirely “new.”

### C5 — “Sea is no more”: evil, not mere geography
**Locus:** on 21:1 (slice ~l. 52)  
**Quote:** "Beale (1999: 1042) lists five uses of the concept in this book… it is likely that the first two predominate. The sea as a symbol of evil would best explain why it is added here… evil will 'be no more.'"  
**Claim:** Osborne prioritizes sea as origin of evil / persecuting nations (with Beale’s five uses noted); false trinity and hostile nations already cast into lake of fire.

### C6 — New Jerusalem: bride simile; people and place
**Locus:** on 21:2 (slice ~ll. 60–64)  
**Quote:** "Is the New Jerusalem the place in which the saints reside, or is it a symbol of the saints themselves?… Babylon was both a people and a place, and that is the better answer here… it represents heaven as both the saints who inhabit it and their dwelling place."  
**Claim:** Surveys Thüsing, Gundry (saints alone / future state not place), Mounce (church perfected as city); Osborne: people in 21:9–10, 13–14; place in 21:3, 7–8, 24, 26. Bride adornment echoes Isa. 54; 61:10; 62:1–5; links 19:7–8 righteous deeds with jewels of 21:18–21.

### C7 — Covenant dwelling / Shekinah; plural “peoples”
**Locus:** on 21:3–4 (slice ~ll. 66–74)  
**Quote:** "The first part of the promise, ἡ σκηνὴ τοῦ θεοῦ… is a virtual translation of 'Shekinah'… finalized in two stages, first when 'the Word became flesh and tabernacled… among us' (John 1:14), and second here… John alone has the plural λαοί, indicating all the peoples of the world… In eternity all ethnic and racial distinctions will disappear, and we will be one."  
**Claim:** Sinai/holiness-code promise fulfilled (Lev. 26; Ezek. 37:27 etc.); tears/death/mourning/crying/pain removed (Isa. 25:8; 7:15–17 anticipation); “former things have passed away” frames 21:1–4; fulfills overcomer promises of chs. 2–3.

### C8 — God’s speech 21:5–8: newness, truthfulness, finished, Alpha/Omega, water freely, overcomer vs coward
**Locus:** on 21:5–8 (slice ~ll. 80–104)  
**Quote:** "καινὰ ποιῶ πάντα… a prophetic present guaranteeing… God’s future re-creation… Γέγοναν… salvation history is at an end… 'Alpha and Omega'… sole origin and goal of all things… To the one who thirsts I will give from the spring of the water of life freely… also an invitation to the unsaved and continues the mission theme… The reader is being asked to make a choice whether to 'overcome'… or to be a 'coward'…"  
**Claim:** Three stages of “finished”: cross (John 19:30), seventh bowl (16:17), eternal end (21:6). Inheritance language unique in book; Davidic covenant language with “God” not “father” reserved for God–Jesus. Vice list (21:8) summarizes book’s sins; first term δειλοῖς especially church members who fail to persevere (Heb. 6; 10; etc. paralleled without adjudicating eternal security).

### C9 — Heaven and earth united one eternal order
**Locus:** Summary 21:1–8 (slice ~ll. 108–114)  
**Quote:** "Heaven in 7:9–17 is almost certainly the same place as the renewed earth of 21:1–22:5… in Revelation heaven and earth are united in one eternal order… When the old heaven and earth are destroyed (20:11; 21:1), the 'new heaven and new earth' (21:1) become one."  
**Claim:** Osborne synthesizes OT higher heaven, intertestamental paradise, Jesus/Paul/Hebrews/2 Peter, then holds Rev. 7 and 21 as same place pictured differently; three intro themes: end of old aeon, bridal theme continued, uniting so God dwells with people.

### C10 — 21:9–27 elaborates 21:1–8; Tale of Two Cities; city becomes temple / Holy of Holies
**Locus:** intro 21:9–27 (slice ~ll. 148–149)  
**Quote:** "Schüssler Fiorenza (1991: 109) shows how extensively 21:9–22:5 elaborates 21:1–8… Beasley-Murray… A Tale of Two Cities: The Harlot and the Bride… in Ezekiel it is the temple itself that is central while in this section there is no temple (21:22), and the city of God is pictured as the temple itself… the city has become the temple, and God’s Shekinah has now been expanded to include the whole dwelling place…"  
**Claim:** Deliberate antithesis with 17:1–19:5 (Krodel synopsis); ABA of harlot–eschaton–bride; church already temple inauguratedly (1 Cor. 3 etc.), heaven finalizes physically.

### C11 — Angelic guide parallels 17:1–3; bride as wife of the Lamb; mountain / from God
**Locus:** on 21:9–10 (slice ~ll. 184–192)  
**Quote:** "Come, I will show you the bride, the wife of the Lamb… sacred marriage has taken place… Of the twenty-nine times Christ is called 'the Lamb'… seven occur in 21:9–22:5… only the sacrificial death of the Lamb… has made all this possible… Behind this passage is undoubtedly Ezek. 40:1–2… Holy City… from God… free gift…"  
**Claim:** Simile→metaphor shift does not collapse city into saints alone; mountain has revelatory function (possibly Zion with 14:1); origin is God’s gift not human good works.

### C12 — Gates/foundations: twelve tribes + twelve apostles; access via whole people of God
**Locus:** on 21:12–14 (slice ~ll. 204–214)  
**Quote:** "the people of God provide access to the 'people' of the world so that they might repent… the twelve tribes as an entity are the gates, and the twelve apostles as an entity are the foundation… entry to the celestial city comes through the whole people of God, Israel and the church."  
**Claim:** Wall for glory not defense; angels over gates not guards but linked to chs. 2–3 angels (Beale); Park’s “eschatologically restored Israel only” for tribes noted but rejected in favor of distinct Israel + church unity (vs merely spiritual tribes). Zodiac-order theory for directions noted as unproven.

### C13 — Measurements: cube = Holy of Holies; symbolic size for all saints
**Locus:** on 21:15–17 (slice ~ll. 216–220)  
**Quote:** "it is a perfect cube… The cube shape matches the shape of the Holy of Holies (20 cubits each direction, 1 Kings 6:20…)… 12,000 stadia… ca. 1,416–1,566 miles… The number is obviously symbolic… a city large enough to hold all the saints… from 'every tribe, language, people, and nation'… wall… 144 cubits… connected with the 144,000… purpose… 'beauty and demarcation' (Krodel)."  
**Claim:** Measuring = ownership/protection (Ezek. 40–48; Zech.); human measure used by angel; size of Roman Empire vs 14:20 Palestine; wall too small for literal 1,500-mile height → symbolic.

### C14 — Jewels: breastplate of high priest preferred; priestly church; contrast harlot
**Locus:** on 21:18–21 (slice ~ll. 228–288)  
**Quote:** "Three major theories… (1) … reverse of… zodiac… (2) … breastplate of the high priest… (3) … general depiction of the glory… This seems the most viable view [breastplate]… the church… end-time Israel, and the high priestly imagery is linked with 1:6; 5:10; and 20:6… contrast… between the harlot and the bride…"  
**Claim:** Kircher/zodiac reverse (R. Charles et al.) “tantalizing” but manuscript-unbacked (Glasson); Beale/Caird semantic-equivalents argument accepted. Transparent gold radiates God’s glory not its own; each gate one huge pearl; street gold (contrasts 11:8 street of great city).

### C15 — No temple (21:22): God and the Lamb are the temple
**Locus:** on 21:22 (slice ~ll. 296–306)  
**Quote:** "And I did not see a temple… he physically resides among his people (Rev. 21:3), and the entire city has been made into a Holy of Holies (21:16)… 'The Lord God Almighty and the Lamb… are its temple.'… Christ the sacrificial Lamb… takes his place alongside God the Father as the temple… unity of God and Christ… now as the temple in the Holy City."  
**Claim:** Background that physical temple not finally needed (Jer. 3:16–17; Jesus John 4:21; Stephen; Heb. 9); Qumran community-as-temple still expected temple in NJ—John goes further; ninth/final “Lord God Almighty.”

### C16 — No sun/moon; nations walk by light; kings bring glory (mission/inclusion, not universalism)
**Locus:** on 21:23–26 (slice ~ll. 308–320)  
**Quote:** "the nations will walk by its light, and the kings of the earth will carry their glory into it… finalizing the theme in the book on the conversion of the nations… John has replaced the idea of military victory and plunder with that of conversion and worship… God’s mercy ultimately triumphs over evil and has redeemed some even from among 'the kings of the earth.'"  
**Claim:** Isa. 60 dominates; gates never shut / no night = evil gone (// sea no more); glory and honor of nations = worship surrendered to God. Additional note (slice ~ll. 346–347): rejects Rissi/Caird-style universalism or conversion from lake of fire; kings converted earlier (e.g. 11:13); 21:27 excludes unclean.

### C17 — Nothing unclean; Lamb’s book of life only entrance
**Locus:** on 21:27 (slice ~ll. 322–334)  
**Quote:** "Nothing unclean and no one who practices abomination and falsehood will ever enter it, but only those who are written in the Lamb’s book of life."  
**Claim:** Two categories (things and people); unclean/abomination/falsehood tied to beast empire and vice lists; Beale’s special stress on false professing believers noted; book written before foundation (17:8), made possible by Lamb’s death (13:8).

### C18 — Final Eden: elevated restored Paradise; river from throne of God and Lamb
**Locus:** intro 22:1–5 + 22:1–2a (slice ~ll. 360–388)  
**Quote:** "Eden has not only been restored but has been elevated and expanded… river of the water of life… flowing from the throne of God and the Lamb down the center of its street… Ezekiel 47 provides the primary background… God and the Lamb are juxtaposed, continuing the major christological theme of the unity of God and Christ as deity."  
**Claim:** Gen. 2 river + Ezek. 47 + Zech. 14:8 + Johannine living water + Rev. 7:17; 21:6 combined; crystal brightness // sea of glass / jasper / transparent gold; throne shifts from inaccessibility (ch. 4) to nearness; 1 Cor. 15:24 and co-regency treated as supplementary not contradictory.

### C19 — Trees of life (collective): twelve fruits monthly; leaves heal the nations
**Locus:** on 22:2b (slice ~ll. 392–400)  
**Quote:** "better to take this as a collective singular… many trees lining both banks… produce… twelve kinds of fruit, yielding its fruit every month… leaves… for healing the nations… does not mean healing is still needed. Rather, it symbolizes the healing that has already occurred… physical healing… and spiritual healing… another reference to the conversion of the nations."  
**Claim:** Fulfills 2:7 paradise promise; goes beyond Ezek. 47 (twelve kinds); particularism of Ezekiel universalized to nations who repented vs destroyed rejecters.

### C20 — No curse; priestly service; see God’s face; name on forehead; reign forever
**Locus:** on 22:3–5 (slice ~ll. 402–418)  
**Quote:** "There is no longer any curse… his slaves will worship and serve him. They will see his face, and his name will be on their foreheads… they will reign forever and ever."  
**Claim:** Zech. 14:11 + Gen. 3 curses + ḥērem judgment removed by Lamb’s blood; λατρεύω = cultic service/worship (// 7:15); Eden work as prototype of tabernacle service (Park/Cassuto/Wenham); three stages of seeing God (Exod. 33:20 → John 1:18 → 22:4); name = ownership/status/protection (// 3:12; 7:3; 14:1); millennial reign (20:4) becomes eternal; Beale: rule over new creation like Adam Gen. 1:28, not literal dominion over other saints/angels.

### C21 — Epilogue frames book with prologue; organization and dual themes
**Locus:** intro 22:6–21 (slice ~ll. 442–448)  
**Quote:** "the close parallels with 1:1–3 demonstrate that 'the author has self-consciously framed the entire composition with similar motifs'… two major themes: the authenticity of the prophecy (22:6, 8, 16, 18–19) and the nearness of the return of Christ (22:7, 10, 12, 20)… Also… warnings and promises given to the seven churches…"  
**Claim:** Lists prologue//epilogue parallels (shown slaves; from God; soon; beatitude; words of prophecy; keep; parousia; faithfulness; Alpha/Omega). Rejects R. Charles’s rearrangement; liturgical-dialogue theories speculative; places 22:6–9 with epilogue (not only conclusion of vision) against Aune/Giblin primacy of 22:6–9 as close of 21:1–22:9. Osborne’s five sections: 6–7; 8–11; 12–19; 20; 21.

### C22 — Authentic words; God of spirits of prophets; “soon” / imminence
**Locus:** on 22:6–7 (slice ~ll. 512–528)  
**Quote:** "These words are faithful and true… show his slaves what must soon take place… 'Behold, I am coming soon. Blessed is the one who keeps the words of the prophecy of this book.'"  
**Claim:** Speaker likely bowl angel of 21:9; quotes 21:5; whole book trustworthy. “Spirits of the prophets” = natural faculties quickened by Spirit (Swete/Fee; // 1 Cor. 14:32). “Soon” = temporal nearness of eschaton (not mere speed); delay problem answered via 2 Pet. 3:8–9 and Beale: next salvation-historical event after death/resurrection/Pentecost is second coming—still “near” even if millennia later. Christ speaks 22:7; sixth beatitude; τηρέω = perseverance/obedience; “purpose of eschatology… is ethics.”

### C23 — Do not worship angel; do not seal; time near; wicked/righteous continue (rhetorical warning)
**Locus:** on 22:8–11 (slice ~ll. 530–556)  
**Quote:** "Don’t seal the words of the prophecy of this book, for the time is near. Let the wicked continue to act wickedly… Let the righteous continue to do righteous deeds…"  
**Claim:** 19:10 // 22:8–9 frame eschaton section; worship God alone = basic message of book. Unsealing reverses 10:4 / Dan. 12:4—eschaton disclosure time. On 22:11 surveys four readings; prefers rhetorical combination of options 1–2 with Beale/Isa. 6:9–10 / Ezek. 3:27: warning not predestination; still time to wash/come (22:14, 17); leaders proclaim, not moral-police, while saints do righteousness/holiness.

### C24 — Coming soon with reward/repayment by works; full Alpha–Omega titles on Christ
**Locus:** on 22:12–13 (slice ~ll. 560–570)  
**Quote:** "Behold, I am coming soon, and my reward is with me to repay all on the basis of their work. I am the Alpha and the Omega, the First and the Last, the Beginning and the End."  
**Claim:** Isa. 40:10; 62:11; Prov. 24:12; μισθός can be reward or punishment; judged by works frequent for both groups; “saved by grace… judged by works”—not justification-by-works. 22:13 only place with all three title types on Christ; ABAB of God/Christ titles completed; sovereignty over history anchors judge/warning.

### C25 — Seventh beatitude: wash robes → tree of life + enter city; dogs outside
**Locus:** on 22:14–15 (slice ~ll. 572–586)  
**Quote:** "God blesses those who wash their robes, with the result that they have authority over the tree of life and enter by its gates into the city. Outside are the dogs, the sorcerers…"  
**Claim:** Ongoing washing (present participle) // 7:14 blood of Lamb; white garments theme; authority over tree > Adam’s mere access. Outside = exclusion/shame (// Heb. 13; Gehenna imagery possible). “Dogs” general for those resisting God (false Christians included, not restricted); loves and practices falsehood climactic (// Satan father of lies).

### C26 — Jesus authenticates: Root/Offspring of David, Morning Star; prophets to churches
**Locus:** on 22:16 (slice ~ll. 588–596)  
**Quote:** "I, Jesus, sent my angel to testify to you about these things concerning the churches. I am the Root and Offspring of David as well as the bright Morning Star."  
**Claim:** ὑμῖν more likely circle of Christian prophets (// 22:9) than churches themselves; messianic Isa. 11 + Num. 24:17; Warrior Messiah power over wicked; ἐγώ εἰμι connotes Yahweh.

### C27 — “Come”: mission invitation to thirsty (primary reading); free water of life
**Locus:** on 22:17 (slice ~ll. 598–606)  
**Quote:** "The Spirit and the bride say, 'Come,' and let the one who hears say, 'Come.' Let the one who thirsts come; let the one who wishes receive the water of life freely."  
**Claim:** Osborne opts (immediate context over larger) for invitation to readers, not primarily cry for Jesus’ parousia—though both themes are central in epilogue; Christ likely speaker of the verse. Spirit = Holy Spirit + Spirit-inspired prophets; bride = end-time church of 21:9–10 vs “one who hears” = current church (1:3; chs. 2–3). Both-and: evangelize unsaved and call straying members (Sardis, Laodicea, Nicolaitan orbits) deeper; Isa. 55:1 // 21:6; eucharistic reading does not fit context well.

### C28 — Warning against adding/subtracting: false teachers; plagues / lose tree and city
**Locus:** on 22:18–19 (slice ~ll. 608–616)  
**Quote:** "If anyone adds to these things, God will add to that person the plagues that are written in this book. If anyone takes away… God will take away that person’s share in the tree of life and in the Holy City…"  
**Claim:** Speaker Jesus (ἐγώ + μαρτυρῶ // 16, 20); Deut. 4:2; 12:32 integrity formula; targets heretical distortion (Nicolaitan idolatry/libertinism; cults restructuring faith), not ordinary interpretive disagreement (pre/post-trib etc.). Directed to every hearer (// 1:3). Lex talionis curses: add→plagues (earthly judgments); take away→lose share in tree/city (second death). Osborne holds real possibility of apostasy (John 15; Heb.; 2 Pet.; 1 John; Rev. 2:5; 3:3; 21:8; 22:18–19) while noting both Calvinist and Arminian frameworks still must warn; distorting message “tantamount to apostasy.”

### C29 — “Yes, I am coming soon”; Amen; Come, Lord Jesus; grace with all
**Locus:** on 22:20–21 (slice ~ll. 618–628)  
**Quote:** "Yes, I am going to come soon. Amen. Come, Lord Jesus. May the grace of the Lord Jesus be with all the readers."  
**Claim:** ναί authenticates; church’s ἔρχου // Marana tha (1 Cor. 16:22; Did. 10.6) with warning context; eucharistic setting for 22:20 rejected as primary (Aune)—parousia desire. Benediction makes book epistle (// 1:4); grace for perseverance; πᾶντων “all” (shortest/hardest reading) expands to saved and unsaved open to the book—fits mission theme.

### C30 — Epilogue synthesis: sovereignty, soon return, conversion + perseverance, authenticity
**Locus:** Summary 22:6–21 (slice ~ll. 626–628)  
**Quote:** "it sums up the key emphases: the sovereignty of God, the soon return of Christ, and the necessity of both conversion for unbelievers and perseverance on the part of believers… the time for decision is today… 'Amen, come, Lord Jesus'… Without his grace, belief and strength to persevere are impossible goals."  
**Claim:** Unidentified speakers deliberate so message not messenger is focus; ethical responsibility under imminent return is epilogue’s horizontal thread.

## Coverage

**Read in full:** entire cache slice R8 (V 21:1–22:5 + VI 22:6–21), including Osborne’s translations, exegesis, summaries/contextualizations, and additional notes for these sections.

**Major blocks covered:**
- 21:1–8 basic vision, throne voice, God speech, overcomer/coward, heaven–earth unity summary  
- New-creation vs renovation survey (Jewish + modern)  
- 21:9–27 Holy of Holies expansion: guide, wall/gates/foundations, cube measures, jewels debate, no temple, light/nations/kings, purity/book of life; anti-universalist note  
- 22:1–5 final Eden: river, trees, no curse, face, name, reign  
- 22:6–21 epilogue: prologue parallels; authenticity; imminence; angel commands; works judgment; beatitude/vice; “Come”; add/subtract; Amen/grace  

**Apparatus:** TC notes sampled where they affect preferred readings (λαοί plural; wash robes vs do commandments; tree not book of life; “all” in benediction); not every minor variant claim-extracted.

**Not present / not forced:** No separate “mission” treatise beyond Osborne’s mission/inclusion threads at 21:6, 21:24–26, 22:2, 22:17, 22:21; no claim inventing material outside this range.
